value.first: He's right on time - 6 months is the window. The method is iron-first solids with early allergen introduction. Two clocks are running: the iron he banked before birth is running low, and waiting on allergens backfires - the LEAP trial found about 80% less peanut allergy in babies who ate it early instead of avoiding it.
value.second: Day 1: sit him fully upright, offer a spoon or two of one iron-rich food - iron-fortified oat cereal, pureed beef, or mashed lentils. Most ends up on the tray; that's a win. Days 2-7: build to iron-rich food twice a day, add mashed veg and fruit. Milk continues as usual - solids add to it, don't replace it. Gagging is noisy and normal; choking is silent.
value.third: Week 2, start allergens: morning, thin half a teaspoon of peanut butter into a puree (never a glob, never whole nuts), tiny taste, wait 10 min, watch 2 hours. Next day, cooked egg. One new allergen a day, then feed each about twice a week - stopping undoes the protection. No honey before 12 months. If he ever has trouble breathing, swelling, or widespread hives after eating, that's an emergency - go now. Tell me how it goes and I'll check in Thursday.
